review.purpose: Use the worker-shipped synthetic population to establish expected groups and withhold evaluation labels from matching.
review.finding: The sample has seven records in four authored groups, with three Smith variants, two Doe variants and two distinct Jones records. The sample is materialized once; customers omits expected_entity, and fixture_truth carries that label only for evaluation. These are worker-project synthetic labels, not an independent benchmark.

review.purpose: Evaluate how a pair-link threshold changes recovered and missed labeled duplicates rather than treating row scores as certainty.
review.finding: The real released resolver materializes seven rows with cluster IDs and scores using three comparison columns and train=false. Every unordered pair is evaluated exactly once; precision is NULL if no pair is grouped. Singleton score 1.0 is kept with explicit context, not interpreted as a probability of uniqueness. The focused 0.9999 experiment changes clustering while retaining sample and labels.
